answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using time-locked slashable staking. Participants deposit bonded collateral at a network inlet to obtain task allocation rights. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of locked capital and slashing risk per identity across an ocean of synthetic nodes. Disputed peers drop into an umber quarantine tier with restricted throughput. However, this mechanism biases the ecosystem toward wealthy cartels and marginalizes capital-poor agents.
